reviews.review: Good game. played the whole main story in co-op. enjoyed it but too much yapping.

Game draws you in with wonderful art and amazing game mechanics... then boom you are crying in a corner because you cant figure out the attack types of the regular mob spawns and you died 16 times trying to cross a bridge before you get to the boss. Please punish me more daddy.

TL;DR - 10/10 experience with friends that has great gameplay, a mountain of puzzles and secrets, and a great build crafting system. Maybe a 9/10 thanks to it's solo experience not quite being the same and a very forgettable - dare I say ignorable - story.

A straight, A+, upgrade of a sequel that you rarely see in the industry. If you have 2 friends to play with and all of you go in blind together, I can't stress this enough - this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ peak. If you play solo, it's just not the same experience - it was definitely designed with co-op in mind. 

-The game is filled to the brim with secrets and puzzles - I sincerely doubt anyone can find every secret this game has to offer in a single blind playthrough. Whole ass dungeons will be behind walls that you can walk past without ever realizing.  Many bosses have multiple different ways of beating them, each way giving you unique rewards that are always super flavorful to the boss specifically. Like the first game, you can have 2 different playthroughs and fight different bosses for most of the run as compared to your previous (save for story bosses). Some bosses are just damage sponges unfortunately, but most of them are still fun either way. Remnant 2 also just has more variety in it's bosses as a whole.
Speaking of bosses and puzzles - the best encounters in this game were far and away the "non" boss fights. The puzzle encounters, or survival encounters, or parkour encounters. So much thought was put into each of them, and if you're playing with friends (and sometimes solo too) you feel like you're in a movie sometimes. On that note, the set-pieces and scenery in this game are incredible. Screenshot a lot and you'll have some pretty solid wallpapers.

-If you're a build crafter like me, know that the abilities, gunplay, and build crafting are definitely my favorite part of the game and the part that makes this game shine as a sequel. The first game gave you guns, and you had the option to change the mods on those guns, and the armor gave you set bonuses. Also a basically useless melee - that's it. Not bad for a solid gunplay experience, but otherwise nothing really there.
 [i] Remnant 2 though? [/i]  First, you have classes now that each have very unique ways of interacting with enemies and gameplay, and you can have 2 active on any given character - note that i say active - you can learn and level up every class in the game on one character. There's way more weapons to play with, many of them having really unique and creative abilities (and each gun has an entirely unique way of firing). Melee weapons are actually crazy good in this game that also have their own unique mods now too. They ditched armor set bonuses in favor of 4 rings, an amulet, and a way to change how your dragon-heart (health flask) works.  All of these combined changes made for some of the most unique buildcrafting I've ever had in a game like this, allowing me to make practically any gameplay style I had in mind. And with a little fine-tuning and tweaking, you can make any build viable, allowing you to play however you want. The fact that there's a firing range in the hub area that allows you to actively track your dps, and 10 (?) loadout slots is amazing, and a great way to build as crazily as you want to and IMMEDIATELY TEST IT. I spent so much time in the firing range making as many builds as I could - and the fact you can do this ALL ON ONE CHARACTER is great. To give an example, had this melee build (an impossibility in the first game, really) that had the best dps and survivability in our whole playthrough that was super fun and flashy, but some enemies are naturally anti-melee, and thankfully i had my friends with their own entirely unique builds to cover my weaknesses. And if they weren't there to help or melee simply wasn't working, I had multiple builds on standby that were each an entirely new way of playing the game and viable in their own rights.  
 
My only complaints would be that some secrets are just nonsensically difficult to get. The dlcs in particular had some secrets that genuinely had me stumped as to how anyone was supposed to figure that out without the help of a wiki. 
Also, the story is garbage - at least, it comes off that way with how awfully the dialogue is written and voice-acted. Me and my friends couldn't have cared less about it by the end, which we really just watched at that point for a good laugh. The lore is fine and existent through logs and stuff, but it never really tries to present itself to you, and the story is bad enough that you just can't even be bothered to go looking for it. The only reason I ever had any piqued interest in the narrative was through the art direction and environments, but reading or hearing one line of text was usually enough to make me go "I actually don't care enough." That being said, the story being bad is inconsequential to the gameplay experiences, though it does suck to imagine what could have been had it been elevated by it instead.

My friends and I already plan to make sure we play Remnant 3 (or it's equivalent) on release, hope it lives up to our hype.
